newsitem.title: USA: CFX to acquire Portsmouth Bank.
newsitem.headline: CFX to acquire Portsmouth Bank.

text.p: CFX Corp said Thursday it had signed a definitive agreement to acquire Portsmouth Bank Shares Inc and its Portsmouth Savings Bank unit in a stock swap.

CFX said that based on the closing price of its common stock on February 12 of $18.50, the indicated value of the deal was $17.58 for each Portsmouth share, putting the value of the transaction at about $106 million.
CFX said each outstanding common share of Portsmouth would be converted into 0.95 share of CFX.
If the average price of CFX common is below $15.70 for the 10 trading days preceding the last regulatory approval required for the merger, the exchange ratio will be 1.05.
The ratio will float between 0.95 and 1.05 if the average price of CFX common is between $17.375 and $15.70.
Portsmouth, based in Portsmouth, N.H., may terminate the agreement if the average price of CFX common is below $14.20, unless CFX agrees to raise the exchange ratio.
CFX said the transaction would be tax-free to shareholders of Portsmouth and is subject to approval by regulators and shareholders of both companies.
As part of the deal, three Portstmouth directors will join the CFX board and two will become directors of CFX Bank, it said.
Peter Baxter, CFX president and chief executive officer, said CFX plans to add significantly to Portsmouth's asset base upon completion of the merger.

He said that after efficiencies resulting from the transaction, and after certain balance sheet restructuring, the deal will increase both earnaings per share and book value per share, making the acquisition beneficial to shareholders of both companies.
He said CFX will take a special charge of about $2.9 million for one-time costs of the transaction.
CFX is a multi-bank holding company. It had assets of $1.6 billion at the end of 1996.
